no-run-as: No acting account is configured, so a converted job would have no identity to run as. A schedule fires with nobody present, and the job's own owner is not used as a fallback. Set the "job_flow_run_as" setting to an existing account first.
run-as-missing: The configured acting account "ghost" is not an existing user, so every flow generated from a job would be refused when saved. Point "job_flow_run_as" at an account that exists.
no-reference: The job carries no uuid, slug or reference, so the generated flow could not record what it was generated from and nobody could trace it back.
zero-interval: interval "0": a schedule trigger needs a cadence, and a job with no positive interval has none to translate.
missing-interval: interval "": a schedule trigger needs a cadence, and a job with no positive interval has none to translate.
odd-interval: interval 7 seconds: a five-field cron is absolute wall-clock time, so only an interval that divides the hour or the day evenly is the same cadence. The expressible intervals are: 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360, 600, 720, 900, 1200, 1800, 3600, 7200, 10800, 14400, 21600, 28800, 43200, 86400. Rounding to the nearest one would change how often this job runs.
schedule-after: scheduleAfter "2026-01-01": a cron expression has no "not before" bound, so a delayed-start job would begin firing on the next tick instead.
single-run: singleRun: a schedule trigger fires for as long as the flow is enabled; there is no "run once and disable myself" in the cron vocabulary.
user-id: userId "anja": a scheduled flow runs as its OWNER — the account that creates it — and a generated document cannot set an owner, so the run identity would silently change.
no-job-class: jobClass is not set, so there is no action for a flow step to stand in for.
ping: jobClass "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\PingAction": a ping calls the Source's own location with no path, and "openconnector.source-call" refuses an empty "endpoint" — it only calls a path RELATIVE to the source, so there is no step that reproduces a bare ping.
event: jobClass "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\EventAction": no flow node emits a CloudEvent onto the event bus, so a generated flow would run green and deliver nothing.
unknown-class: jobClass "OCA\Other\Job": no flow node stands in for this action. Only "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\SynchronizationAction" and "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\FlowAction" have decomposed equivalents.
legacy-class-name: jobClass "OCA\OpenConnector\Action\SynchronizationAction": no flow node stands in for this action. Only "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\SynchronizationAction" and "OCA\Integriq\Service\Job\FlowAction" have decomposed equivalents.
flow-no-target: arguments.flowId is not set: "openregister.sub-flow" needs a flow to run.
flow-extra-arguments: arguments extra, more: nothing in the generated flow reads them, and an argument the action used but the step ignores is exactly a flow that does less while reporting success.
sync-no-target: arguments.synchronizationId is not set: "openconnector.synchronization-run" must name a configured synchronization, and this step never creates one.
everything: The job carries no uuid, slug or reference, so the generated flow could not record what it was generated from and nobody could trace it back.
